headline: Leptospirosis Cases Rise to 6,253 as DOH Monitors Post-Flood Surge
seoTitle: Philippines Leptospirosis Cases Rise to 6,253, Deaths Reach 378 | FMB News
seoDescription: DOH data show 6,253 leptospirosis cases and 378 deaths nationwide, with recent infections rising sharply after flooding and Metro Manila hospital beds heavily occupied.
deck: The Department of Health says 6,253 leptospirosis cases and 378 deaths have been recorded nationwide, while recent infections rose sharply after widespread flooding and hospital pressure remains high in Metro Manila.
author: FMB News Desk

continuesFrom.headline: DOH Records 5,835 Leptospirosis Cases Nationwide as Flood Exposure Drives Recent Rise
continuesFrom.whatChanged: DOH's national tally has increased from 5,835 cases and 358 deaths in FMB News's September 1 report to 6,253 cases and 378 deaths. New DOH data also show a sharp recent two-week rise and heavy occupancy of dedicated leptospirosis beds in Metro Manila.

sections.heading: What changed
paragraphs: The Department of Health now reports 6,253 leptospirosis cases nationwide, with 378 deaths recorded from January 4 through August 29, 2026. FMB News's September 1 report carried the earlier national tally of 5,835 cases and 358 deaths.
The updated figures are a material continuation because they add 418 reported cases and 20 deaths to the earlier count and include new evidence of a steep post-flood rise in recent infections.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: DOH data cited by the Philippine News Agency, INQUIRER.net and The Philippine STAR show that 6,253 leptospirosis cases have been recorded nationwide so far this year. The total remains 12 percent lower than the comparable period in 2025, but the recent trend moved sharply upward after prolonged flooding.

DOH Undersecretary Gloria Balboa said 824 cases were recorded from August 2 to 15, up 77 percent from 465 cases in the preceding monitoring period. The department is closely monitoring regions with rising case trends and areas that have breached epidemic thresholds.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Leptospirosis is a bacterial infection commonly associated with exposure to water or soil contaminated by the urine of infected animals. Flooding raises the risk because residents, workers and responders may have unavoidable contact with contaminated water.

As of 6 p.m. on September 3, DOH reported 602 dedicated leptospirosis beds across 20 DOH hospitals in Metro Manila, including 260 additional surge beds. Of that capacity, 562 beds were occupied. The department said referrals and patient redistribution were continuing, especially for patients who need dialysis or higher-level care.

DOH also said regional health offices had distributed or augmented 1.2 million doxycycline capsules to affected areas, with additional stocks held by Centers for Health Development and DOH hospitals. Antibiotics should not be self-administered without medical advice because proper timing, dosing and contraindications matter.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The national year-to-date count is still below last year's comparable total, but the recent surge shows why flood exposure remains a major health risk even after water levels begin to recede. The illness can progress rapidly and severe cases may require dialysis or intensive hospital care.
The high occupancy of dedicated beds in Metro Manila also matters because another wave of post-flood infections can increase pressure on referral hospitals and emergency services.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for the next DOH epidemiological update, changes in the death toll, new regional epidemic-threshold breaches and whether Metro Manila hospitals add further surge capacity.

FMB News will also track whether the recent case increase continues after the incubation period associated with the latest flooding and whether additional prevention or treatment advisories are issued.

audit.socialCaption: UPDATE: DOH now reports 6,253 leptospirosis cases and 378 deaths nationwide. The year-to-date total remains below 2025, but recent infections rose sharply after widespread flooding, while 562 of 602 designated leptospirosis beds in 20 DOH Metro Manila hospitals were occupied as of Sept. 3. This continues FMB News's Sept. 1 report.
verificationNotes: The central figures, 6,253 cases and 378 deaths, are attributed to Department of Health data and corroborated by PNA, INQUIRER.net and The Philippine STAR.
The article distinguishes the lower year-to-date comparison with 2025 from the sharp recent increase in cases, avoiding the misleading claim that the entire year is worse than last year.
Hospital-capacity figures are time-stamped to 6 p.m. on September 3 and are not presented as real-time occupancy.
The story is a material continuation of FMB News's September 1 article and preserves the original report intact.
The continuation uses the earliest verified live FMB canonical URL and states exactly what changed.
The hero image and required crops are FMB-owned editorial graphics using the approved icon and purple-violet/plum visual system; no documentary photograph was fabricated.
